newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Macri/Galicia win post office bidding.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Macri/Galicia win post office bidding.

text.p: An Argentine consortium of the Grupo Macri-controlled companies Itron and Sideco and Banco de Galicia, with the British Post Office, won the bids Thursday to run the state postal service.

It won a second round of bidding for a 30-year concession by offering a $51.6 million six-monthly fee, beating a rival offer of $48.5 million by the Argentine companies TAC, Roman, Samuel Liberman together with Germany's state post office.

The winning consortium had offered $51 million for state post office Encotesa in Monday's bid-opening, which had to go to a second round because there was a difference of less than the 5.0 percent required with the second highest bid of $48.5 million. A lower third bid of $30.77 million was also made.
Itron has a 46.5 percent stake in the winning consortium, Sideco 41 percent and Banco Galicia 12.5 percent.

"We will improve the postal service in all aspects with a wider range of services," Itron President Luis Cudmani said. "We'll invest in technology and training to give Argentines a postal service comparable with other countries in the world."

Consultants to the winning group made much out of the room for improvement in Argentina's state postal service Encotesa, in a country where 30 letters are sent per person per year compared to 300 in a European country like France.
"Productivity per employee in the Argentine post is 20,000 pieces per year. In the United States it's more like 80,000," said one consultant, who asked not to be named.
Encotesa's annual turnover is about $500 million.

David Roberts of the British Post Office's consultancy arm, technical advisor to the winning consortium, told Reuters that work would begin immediately with nine Post Office experts getting on a plane for Buenos Aires Friday.

"I am totally convinced we came along with technically the best offer," said the general manager of the British Postal Consultancy Service, adding that "matters like efficiency and quality" would be priorities when the new management takes over Encotesa in September.
